mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY growth exceeds 2% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which negatively impacts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises by more than 0.5% in a month and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate activity (HOUST) signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST shows a sustained increase and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals supply chain disruptions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO declines by more than 1% in a month and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) is rising, the combination signals a tightening monetary policy with inflationary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL YoY growth > 2% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real final sales (RSAFS) signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS shows a sustained increase and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, a decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a potential pause or reversal in tightening, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS decreases during a tightening cycle and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.
